solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remarkable old film director is making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means these letters travel in the opposite direction, read right to left

parts.note: Fritz Lang, director of Metropolis
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran film-maker is returning to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Fritz Lang directed Metropolis; 'making a comeback' turns his name and 'is' right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something signal is striking or notable, a slightly formal adjective sense.

clue.text: Jolly poke in the nether regions?

parts.note: jokingly, the lower leg, a shin being well down the body
a dig is a prod or poke

explanation.surface: A cheeky jab somewhere below the belt, passed off as harmless fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nether regions' suggests something ruder; here it is merely the shin, low on the leg, and a poke at it is a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolly is British slang for a party or outing, as is a lively celebration of that name.

clue.text: Angry gardener catches one loaded with pineapples once

definitions.note: a soldier who formerly carried grenades, which were nicknamed pineapples for their shape

indicators.note: catching something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other
an angry person is worked up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A furious gardener grabs someone carrying an armful of pineapples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry' rearranges GARDENER, which 'catches' I. 'Pineapple' was soldiers' slang for a hand grenade.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadiers were originally soldiers specially trained to throw grenades, slangily called pineapples.

clue.text: 14 is wearing make up right now

indicators.note: a piece that wears another has it on, so the second piece is wrapped inside the first

parts.note: to atone is to make up for a wrong
the answer to 14 down is the temperature scale, abbreviated C

explanation.surface: Someone is putting on cosmetics right this minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is CELSIUS, abbreviated C; 'is wearing' puts ATONE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, without any delay, exactly the sense of the clue's idiom.

clue.text: A cry for help brings in top firefighter

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
to top is to beat or best someone

explanation.surface: A shout for assistance summons the leading fire officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firefighter' wants to be a person; it is the fireproof mineral. 'brings in' puts the synonym of 'top' inside the distress call.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral was long used as fireproofing material, so it fights fire in a playful sense.

clue.text: Scuttle stays in kitchen, hidden

indicators.note: the word hidden tells us the letters are concealed within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A coal scuttle stays tucked away in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuttle' looks like a coal bucket in the kitchen scene; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle a ship is to scupper it deliberately so it goes under, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Second person runs further always

parts.note: Eve, the second human in Genesis after Adam
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
more means further, additional

explanation.surface: A grammatical second person keeps running further and further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' looks like grammar ('you'), but it is Eve, created after Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic synonym: forever, for all time to come.

clue.text: Perhaps watch sphere rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a remit is a sphere of responsibility

explanation.surface: Gazing at a globe as it ascends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns REMIT upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one example of a device that measures time, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: She works with Poly making viewing device

indicators.note: letters that are worked are kneaded and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman at the polytechnic builds an optical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges SHE + POLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A small aperture in a door through which one can peep at callers is a means of seeing out.

clue.text: Chilly compartment of larynx, not very old

indicators.note: not means the following pieces are left out of the word for the larynx

parts.note: the larynx is the voice box

explanation.surface: A cold section of the throat, as if part of an aging voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes V and O from VOICEBOX.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator, or a cold section in one, kept cold for food storage.

clue.text: Ill-advised US enemy left abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An unwise American foe deserted on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges US ENEMY + L.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or unbecoming conduct is ill-judged, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Barking Liberal, he raised points in paper

definitions.note: Louis, the blind Frenchman who devised a tactile writing system of raised dots

indicators.note: barking means mad, so these letters go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: A mad Liberal politician made his case in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' (British slang for mad, also a London district) rearranges LIBERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis invented the tactile alphabet of raised dots embossed on paper for blind readers.

clue.text: Coroner's document? Sure thing

definitions.meaning: humorously, a certificate for someone deceased
a racing term for a horse certain to win

explanation.surface: The coroner's paperwork is a foregone conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase is a death certificate; idiomatically it is a certainty.

clue.text: Rudimentary state annihilated by Rome

indicators.note: destroyed letters are broken up and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A primitive realm wiped out by the Roman Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annihilated' rearranges BY ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism at its earliest stage of development, figuratively anything undeveloped.

clue.text: Inventor of scale also adapted sluices

indicators.note: something adapted is altered, so these letters are changed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An engineer who devised a measuring system also modified some floodgates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges SLUICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders, the Swedish astronomer, devised the centigrade temperature scale.

clue.text: Reach a good deal, ignoring bar

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so the next word is removed

parts.note: a bargain is a good deal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting to an agreement while disregarding the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' takes BAR from BARGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain a place is to arrive at or attain it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Writer's got rake fixed outside, not far off

indicators.note: outside means these letters are placed around the setter's contraction
fixed in the sense of rigged or doctored, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the writer's got means 'I have', contracted

explanation.surface: A writer's garden rake has been repaired out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's got' is 'I've got'; 'got' goes into the fodder. 'fixed' rearranges GOT RAKE, placed 'outside' IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for approximately, allowing a small margin either way.

clue.text: A tax is raised, designed to exclude a place with beds

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out the lone letter that follows

parts.note: meant means intended or designed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A levy is imposed, meant to bar a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is raised' reverses TOLL; 'to exclude' takes A from MEANT, leaving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented plot of land where British householders grow vegetables in beds.

clue.text: Dictator broadcasts to Macron

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An autocrat is broadcasting to the French president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasts' rearranges TO MACRON.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat ruling alone, a single absolute ruler.

clue.text: Clue that leads to me, 16, …

definitions.note: the answer to 16 across, an idiom for approximately

parts.note: the answer, read as an instruction, says take the word more without or, which leaves these two letters

explanation.surface: A self-referential riddle pointing on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read as wordplay, the answer says take MORE less OR, which gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean roughly or approximately, so they are interchangeable phrases.

clue.text: Artist makes a mess with it

indicators.note: makes, beside a mess, tells us the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter creates chaos with his materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a mess' signals the shuffle while supplying A MESS; with IT it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri, the French painter, leader of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: … as well as small cross

definitions.meaning: in addition to, as a preposition
the addition sign is a little cross

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, plus a tiny crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means together with, and its symbol is a small upright cross.

clue.text: Rider's heading off in south-east for salmon

indicators.note: in means the shortened rider sits inside the compass letters

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a jockey rides racehorses

explanation.surface: A rider leaves the south-east to go salmon fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes J from JOCKEY, leaving OCKEY, placed 'in' SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific species of red-fleshed fish, a specific example.

clue.text: Book flight

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Reserving a seat on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament book narrates the Israelites' mass departure from Egypt.

clue.text: Big shot Young Conservative fills town up north

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so this piece sits within the other

parts.note: toon is northern English dialect for town, used of Newcastle
YC, abbreviation for a member of the Tory youth wing

explanation.surface: A rising Tory star takes over a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up north' looks like a reversal sign; it marks the dialect word TOON (Newcastle's nickname), which YC 'fills'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy, powerful business magnate is an important person.

clue.text: Form of sugar youngster is chewing initially

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior Scout

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A child is munching on a lump of sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'is chewing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar commonly comes shaped as lumps with six square faces, describing its shape.

clue.text: Who in Paris has toxic mix of the ideal and the chivalrous?

definitions.text: of the ideal and the chivalrous

parts.note: qui is French for who

indicators.note: a mix is a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Which Parisian blends idealism and chivalry into a poisonous brew?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who in Paris' asks for French: qui. 'mix' shuffles 'toxic' to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Don Quixote, the adjective means romantically idealistic and chivalrous.

clue.text: Such airs oddly make a mark

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Such pretensions leave a lasting impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks alternate letters of 'Such airs'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scar is to leave a lasting blemish on skin or a surface.

clue.text: Flyer follows boat to take off

indicators.note: follows means the first piece named comes after the second

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a boat
a tract or flyer is a printed leaflet

explanation.surface: An aircraft trails a boat as it prepares to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' and 'take off' paint aviation; the flyer is a leaflet, and take off is arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to deduct a number, taking it away from another.

clue.text: Notice woman's beginning to employ stick

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An advertisement starting a woman's job hunt stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes the first letter of 'employ'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay attached, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Men with guns go after alien group of badgers and the like

indicators.note: go after means this piece is placed after the preceding ones

parts.note: ET, the film extraterrestrial
a cete is the collective noun for badgers
RA, the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Gunmen pursue an alien and a band of badgers.
explanation.walkthrough: CETE is a rare collective noun for badgers; RA is the British army's Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means and other similar things, used at the end of a list.

clue.text: Fly back east twice, having mislaid articles

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse
having mislaid means some letters are lost from the doubled word
twice means the word is written two times

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, taken two times

explanation.surface: An insect flies back east repeatedly after losing some items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives EASTEAST; 'having mislaid' the two A's leaves ESTEST, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.
